title: Complete proof of Erdős Problem #1095: The Erdős-Selfridge Function

problemStatement.formal: g(k) := \min \{n > k+1 : \text{every prime factor of } \binom{n}{k} \text{ exceeds } k\}
problemStatement.plain: Estimate the Erdős-Selfridge function g(k): the smallest n > k+1 such that every prime factor of the binomial coefficient C(n,k) is greater than k. Concrete values: g(2)=6, g(3)=g(4)=7, g(5)=23, g(6)=143.
whyMatters: Probes the interplay between binomial coefficients and prime factorization at the boundary of computability.
The conjecture log g(k) ~ k/log k (Erdős-Lacampagne-Selfridge 1993) is a sharp version of the bound problem and remains open.
Connects to Sylvester-Schur theorem and arithmetic of factorials (binomial coefficients of small arguments cannot be smooth).

proven: Lower bound: g(k) >> exp(c·(log k)²) (Konyagin 1999, Bull. London Math. Soc. 31)
Upper bound: g(k) <= exp((1+o(1))·k) (Ecklund-Erdős-Selfridge 1974, Math. Comp. 28)
Concrete values: g(2)=6, g(3)=7, g(4)=7, g(5)=23, g(6)=143 (formalized as theorems in Erdos1095Problem.lean)
open: Sharp asymptotic: log g(k) ~ k/log k (Erdős-Lacampagne-Selfridge 1993 conjecture)
Closing the gap between Konyagin lower bound exp((log k)²) and EES upper bound exp(k)
knownResults.goal: Eliminate axioms g, g_gt, g_spec, g_minimal by building g constructively via Nat.find on the (decidable) condition (n > k+1 ∧ binomIsKRough n k); requires proving existence first via Kummer/Sylvester-Schur in Mathlib.
